newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain's Prescott cuts short HK visit.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Prescott cuts short HK visit.

text.p: The deputy leader of the British Labour Party, John Prescott, said on Monday he had been forced to cut short his visit to Hong Kong in order to return home and vote.

"I was to spend three days here in Hong Kong. I am being dragged back for the voting tonight in the House of Commons and a special vote to take place tomorrow," Prescott, who just finished a visit to China, told reporters before returning to London.
Prescott expressed enthusiasm for an early election.

"I would like the general election to take place as soon as possible and, indeed, by going back today if we could defeat the government tomorrow, I would hope to see possibly a general election as soon as possible," he said.
The Labour Party is widely expected to win the next general election, which must be held by May 22 at the latest.
